title: An npm sync installs a dist-tag, which can move the pin backwards
foundBy: deps-maintenance campaign, pilots 1 and 2: the pilot2 orchestrator's findings (campaign-workspaces/deps-maintenance/pilot2/archives/deps-pilot2-20260922T203209Z/orchestrator/output/findings.md) and the step corrections pilot3's coordination.md section 5 carries

evidence.verified:
`make ci` passed at 10cc896, with 111 unit tests where main had 95, and with the end-to-end run of the action. `test_an_internal_npm_pin_names_the_build_of_the_head_commit` and `test_a_sibling_pin_installs_the_build_of_its_head_commit_not_a_tag` fail on the old code.

The collector's run of 2026-09-22T22:07:49Z over all nine projects names no dist-tag. Each of its 5 npm syncs installs the exact version the registry built from the head commit.

The ui action syncing ledger ran verbatim in a clean clone. It moved `package.json` and `package-lock.json` to the build of ledger's head, which `npx cs-ledger version` printed, and `npm run check` exited 0.

resolution: The resolver reads the registry's versions for an internal npm pin and records the one built from the head commit as `lag.version`. An npm sync installs that version exactly, and says it is waiting when the registry holds none.
details: An npm `sync` action emits `npm install --save-exact <package>@dev` for `@codesweep-ai/ui` and `@latest` for every other sibling. A tag moves, and the action means one version: the build of the commit in `lag.head`. On 2026-09-22 `@codesweep-ai/ledger@latest` was the build of 2026-09-15, older than the build of 2026-09-20 that ui pins, so `ui:sync:ledger-npm-codesweep-ai-ledger` run as printed moves the pin backwards. Through cs-npmrevs a tag other than `latest` answers npmjs.com's version rather than a campaign's.
